candidates.tagline: FIFA told Levi's to hide its logo. The tarp made it more famous.
candidates.story: FIFA's 'clean venue' rule forced Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara to wrap its iconic batwing logo in a white tarp for the World Cup — but the tarp preserved the logo's distinctive silhouette so perfectly that the covered version went viral worldwide, becoming more recognisable than the original.
candidates.why_funny: A rule designed to erase a brand from billions of TV screens instead turned that brand into the most-discussed logo at the tournament — Levi's even swapped their Instagram profile picture to the covered version.
candidates.alt: The exterior of Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara showing the iconic red batwing logo tightly wrapped in a white tarp, the distinctive two-wing silhouette still clearly visible through the covering despite FIFA's clean-venue rules

candidates.tagline: Mexico City hung a chandelier in the metro. The drains still flood.
candidates.story: Mexico City installed a chandelier and Victorian wall lamps in its Hidalgo metro station for the World Cup, triggering a viral wave of mocking memes as residents arrived in ball gowns, Napoleon costumes and Beauty and the Beast outfits — while critics pointed out the city's underpasses still flood and its transit infrastructure still crumbles.
candidates.why_funny: The city dressed up its broken metro with a chandelier to impress the world, so residents helpfully dressed up too.
candidates.alt: Commuters walking through Mexico City's Hidalgo metro station beneath a newly installed chandelier and rows of decorative Victorian-style wall lamps added for the 2026 World Cup, the ornate lighting incongruous against the worn station infrastructure
